name: clusters a separable dataset reproducibly
input: two runs over a separable two-cluster dataset
test:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, 2.0], [8.0, 8.0], [9.0, 9.0]])
original = X.copy()
first_centroids, first_labels = kmeans(X, 2, 20, seed=7)
second_centroids, second_labels = kmeans(X, 2, 20, seed=7)
assert np.array_equal(first_centroids, second_centroids)
assert np.array_equal(first_labels, second_labels)
assert first_centroids.shape == (2, 2)
assert first_labels.shape == (4,)
assert np.array_equal(X, original)
assert np.allclose(np.sort(first_centroids, axis=0), [[1.5, 1.5], [8.5, 8.5]])

name: returns finite centroids and nearest-centroid labels
input: duplicate input rows with more centroids than occupied groups
test:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[3.0, -1.0], [3.0, -1.0], [3.0, -1.0]])
centroids, labels = kmeans(X, 3, 5, seed=2)
assert centroids.shape == (3, 2)
assert labels.shape == (3,)
assert np.isfinite(centroids).all()
assert np.issubdtype(labels.dtype, np.integer)
assert ((0 <= labels) & (labels < 3)).all()
distances = ((X[:, None, :] - centroids[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(axis=2)
assert np.allclose(distances[np.arange(len(X)), labels], distances.min(axis=1))

name: computes the mean for a single cluster
input: a one-dimensional dataset with k equal to one
test:
import numpy as np
X = np.array([[0.0], [0.1], [9.9], [10.0]])
centroids, labels = kmeans(X, 1, 20, seed=1)
assert centroids.shape == (1, 1)
assert np.allclose(centroids, [[5.0]])
assert np.array_equal(labels, np.zeros(4, dtype=int))
